Singh Hora, learned counsel for the applicant.
Shri Ravikant Patidar, learned Govt. Advocate for the respondent/State.
Heard on I.A. No.74/2020, an application for exemption from surrendering before the trial Court on account of acute medical ailments along with prayer to hear this revision.

Learned senior counsel submits that the applicant has been convicted and sentenced by the Court of JMFC, Jabalpur in RCT No.13552/2011 against which applicant preferred an appeal registered as Criminal Appeal No.210/2015 and co-accused Harish Dayani and Mohd. Saleem also preferred an appeal registered as Criminal Appeal No.09/2015.

Learned appellate Court heard both the appeal analogously and vide judgment dated 30/12/2019 acquitted co-accused Harish Dayani and Mohd. Saleem, however,
affirmed the conviction and sentence passed against applicant- Nirmal Sen.

sentences.text: 1 Court granted ten days' time to the applicant to surrender before the trial Court, hence the applicant filed this criminal revision against the judgment of appellate Court without surrendering before the trial Court.

It is also submitted by learned senior counsel that the applicant is facing a serious ailment, in general language suffering from prostate cancer with stricture urethra and undergone multiple cystoscopies and dilation.

It is difficult for him to appear before the trial Court and prays to exempt the applicant from surrendering before the trial Court or Police and further prays to hear this revision in absence of surrendering the applicant before the trial Court.
 Perused the documents filed along with this revision specially the order sheets of the appellate Court.

The appellate Court vide order dated 04/12/2019 exempted the applicant on the ground that he appeared on wheel chair in the Court, he is not able to walk normally and after hearing both the parties delivered the judgment on 30/12/2019 affirming the conviction and sentence passed by the Court of JMFC against the applicant and dismissed the appeal so far as applicant is concerned.

Since the appellant was not present before the appellate Court at the time of pronouncement of judgment, he was directed to appear within a period of ten days before the trial Court to undergo the sentence.

It is clearly reflected from the order that learned appellate Court on the date of pronouncement of judgment cancelled the bail- bonds of the applicant and directed him  3 to appear before the trial Court within ten days.

This Court is of the view that such type of direction is not in the shape that learned Nirmal Sen vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 9 January, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/189924179/

Rule 48 of High Court of Madhya Pradesh Rules, 2008 reads as under :
 "48. A memorandum of appeal or revision petition  against conviction, except in cases where the sentence  has been suspended by the Court below, shall contain  a declaration to the effect that the convicted person is  in custody or has surrendered after the conviction.

entities.text: High Court of Madhya Pradesh Rules, 2008

sentences.text: Where the sentence has been so suspended, the  factum of such suspension and its period shall be  stated in the memorandum of appeal or revision  petition, as also in the application under Section 389  of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973.
An application under Section 389 of the Code of  Criminal Procedure, 1973 shall, as far as possible, be  in Format No.11 and shall be accompanied by
an  affidavit of the appellant/applicant or some other  person acquainted with the facts of the case

. "
 4  Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Vivek Rai and another Vs. High Court of Jharkhand, (2015) 12 SCC 86,
clearly explained that in exceptional cases where the applicant is suffering from some grievous diseases and admitted in the hospital, revision can be entertained.

sentences.text: In these circumstances, considering the illness of the applicant and as observed by the appellate Court in the order sheet, this Court finds exceptional case of the applicant and without surrendering before the trial Court entertain this criminal revision against the impugned judgment.

So far as exemption from surrendering of the applicant is concerned, it reveals that he is neither released on bail bonds nor exempted from his arrest till ten days, this Court is not inclined to provide exemption to the applicant for surrendering before the trial Court.
In view of aforesaid, I.A. No.74/2020 is partly allowed to the extent as indicated above.
Now heard both the parties on the point of admission.
5  Learned senior counsel for the applicant as well as learned Govt. Advocate submit that they are ready to argue the matter finally today at the motion stage.
Record of both the Courts below have been received.
At the request of learned counsel for the parties, heard the matter finally at the motion stage.
ORDER At the outset, learned senior counsel for the applicant submits that he is not pressing much on the point of conviction, however, he is merely pressing this revision on the point of sentence.

sentences.text: 3. The case of prosecution, in short, is that the applicant is the person who was nominated by the Hindustan Lever Limited Company under Sub-section (2) of Section 17 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (hereinafter referred to as 'PFA Act') to bear responsibility on behalf of the company for any offence under the PFA Act.
Company prepared Vanaspati Ghee, Khajoor Brand and it was kept in the godown of Lipton India Ltd.
H.D. Dubey, the then Food Inspector of District Flying Squade, Jabalpur went to the godown of Lipton India Limited where he found stock of Dalda Vanaspati Khajoor Brand Ghee kept in a cartoon.

He after purchasing the products and after completing the formalities, sent the same for examination to the Public Analyst and after receiving report another sample was sent to Central Food Laboratory (hereinafter referred to 'CFL').

In these packets, Food Inspector also found that there was no declaration of label, batch, number, month and year of packing as provided under Rule 32 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, 1955.
CFL found that melting point of the Vanaspati Ghee was higher than the normal range 31 to 41 degree Centigrade.
In this respect found the Vanaspati Ghee adulterate and misbranding.
After completion of whole process submitted a complaint against the company and applicant along with 26 persons.

4. Later on, the matter travelled upto Hon'ble Supreme Court on the ground that the person who is nominated by the company i.e. Hindustan Lever Limited, is responsible for the offence under the provisions of PFA Act.

Hon'ble Supreme Court found that the applicant was a nominated person under Section 17(2) of the PFA Act, hence exonerated all the Directors and partners of the company and the applicant on behalf of Hindustan Lever Limited was held responsible to be prosecuted before the trial Court along with Company- Hindustan Lever Limited.
5. The applicant remained absent before the Court of JMFC.
Learned Court of JMFC passed the judgment on 10/12/2014 against the Lipton India Limited, Mohd. Saleem, Harish Dayani and kept pending the case against Hindustan Lever Limited and the applicant.

When the applicant appeared before the Court of JMFC, then after hearing both the parties, the Court of JMFC passed judgment dated 16/06/2015 only against the applicant and not considered the accusation against Hindustan Lever Limited.
It may be due to lost of sight because the case was pending before the trial Court since 1989.
Had the applicant appeared on the date of 10/12/2014, the judgment would have been passed against Hindustan Lever Limited too.

The applicant raised this lacuna in appeal and prayed therein to acquit him on the ground that Company-Hindustan Lever Limited has not been convicted in this case to which applicant is a nominated person for business affairs, however, learned appellate Court has not properly discussed this fact in para-31 of its judgment.
6. Perused the judgment of learned trial Court.
Learned trial Court neither acquitted the company- Hindustan Lever Limited to which the applicant was the nominated person nor exonerated the company of the offences.

Section 17 (1) (a) (b) reads as under :

5 "17. Offences by companies.-- (1) Where an offence under this Act has been committed by a company -- (a) (i) the person, if any, who has been nominated under sub-section (2) to be in charge of, and responsible to, the company for the conduct of the business of the company (hereafter in this section referred to as the person responsible), or (ii) where no person has been so nominated, every person who at the time the offence was committed was in charge of, and was responsible to, the company for the conduct of the business of the company; and (b) the company, shall be deemed to be guilty of the offence and shall be liable to be proceeded against and punished accordingly:
Provided that nothing contained in this sub- section shall render any such person liable to any punishment provided in this Act if he proves that the offence was committed without his knowledge and that he exercised all due diligence to prevent the commission of such offence."

sentences.text: On bare perusal of the provisions of above section, if any product manufactured by the company found to be adulterated, the company as well as nominated person shall be deemed to be guilty of the offence described in Section 17(1) of the PFA Act.

7. The applicant clearly raised objection before learned appellate Court that learned trial Court has not convicted the company-Hindustan Lever Limited, therefore, the appellant being nominated person of the company, could not be held guilty of any offence if company is not held guilty.

Considering this fact, this Court is of the view that learned trial Court in its order sheet dated 10/12/2014 kept pending decision against the company- Hindustan Lever Limited and the applicant because both were not present on the date of 10/12/2014.

When the applicant appeared, then learned trial Court proceeded and delivered judgment against the applicant, however, did not discuss anything about the accusation of company- Hindustan Lever Limited that had been arrayed as an accused.
When applicant raised this point before learned appellate Court, learned appellate Court has also not appreciated this fact in proper perspective.

Since it was a statutory requirement under Section 17(1) of PFA that if the offence is committed by any company, the company is held liable for that offence along with nominated person of the company or who is responsible for the conduct of the business of the company.
8. If the company-Hindustan Lever Limited is acquitted of the charges, the said benefit will also directly go to the applicant.

In view whereof, this Court finds a glaring and patent defect in the judgment of the trial Court as well as in the judgment of the appellate Court, thus, this Court, in these premises, finds it fit to interfere in the judgment of the trial Court in exercise of the revisional jurisdiction under Section 401(1) of Cr.P.C., hence, this Court is inclined to set aside the conviction and sentence passed against the applicant being a nominated person of the company and remitted back the matter to the trial Court for passing fresh judgment considering the company- Hindustan Nirmal Sen vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 9 January, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/189924179/

9. In view of aforesaid discussions, this revision is allowed.

The impugned conviction and sentence passed against the applicant is hereby set aside and the matter is remitted back to the trial Court to revisit the evidence adduced by both the parties and also revisit its judgment dated 16/06/2015, so far as it relates with the applicant and company-Hindustan Lever Limited thereafter again pass a separate judgment after providing opportunity of hearing to the applicant as well as the company- Hindustan Lever Limited without getting prejudice with the discussions made by the appellate Court and this Court.
10. As this case is pending since 1989
, hence, trial Court is expected to conclude the trial within two months after receiving copy of this order.

11. The applicant is directed to appear before the trial Court on 28th January, 2020 and submit bail bonds before the trial Court for his regular appearance as per the previous order on which he was enlarged on bail.
12. Office is directed to send record of the trial Court along with copy of order of this Court as expeditiously as possible.
